CLINICAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Sex: Male
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

REFERRAL INFORMATION
Referring Clinician: Dr [redacted name]
Referral Reason: Elevated total cholesterol 7-8 mmol/L, referred for Familial Hypercholesterolaemia testing

CLINICAL DETAILS
This adult male patient presents with persistently elevated total cholesterol levels ranging from 7-8 mmol/L. Clinical assessment has raised suspicion of Familial Hypercholesterolaemia.

METHODOLOGY
Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed to detect sequence variants and exon deletions/duplications in the following genes:
- LDLR (NM_000527.5): Full gene analysis
- PCSK9 (NM_174936.4): Full gene analysis  
- LDLRAP1 (NM_015627.3): Full gene analysis
- APOB (NM_000384.3): Targeted analysis of exon 26

Analysis was performed using parallel sequencing following target capture by hybridization. Read depth analysis was utilized for detection of exon-level copy number alterations. All identified pathogenic variants were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

Minimum coverage achieved: 30x for >99% of target regions
Mean coverage: 250x

RESULTS

Gene: LDLR (NM_000527.5)
Variant: c.1118_1121dupGTGG p.(Tyr375fs)
Zygosity: Heterozygous
Classification: Pathogenic (ACMG/AMP criteria: PVS1, PM2, PP5)

This frameshift duplication results in premature termination of the LDL receptor protein, leading to loss of function.

No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in:
- LDLRAP1 (NM_015627.3)
- PCSK9 (NM_174936.4)
- APOB exon 26 (NM_000384.3)

SUMMARY
Molecular genetic testing has identified a heterozygous pathogenic frameshift variant c.1118_1121dupGTGG p.(Tyr375fs) in the LDLR gene. This variant confirms the clinical diagnosis of Familial Hypercholesterolaemia (FH).

The LDLR gene encodes the low-density lipoprotein receptor, which plays a crucial role in cholesterol homeostasis by mediating the endocytosis of cholesterol-rich LDL particles. Loss-of-function variants in LDLR account for approximately 85-90% of molecularly confirmed FH cases.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
This frameshift variant in LDLR confirms the diagnosis of heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolaemia. Individuals with heterozygous FH have significantly elevated LDL cholesterol levels from birth and, if untreated, have a greater than 50% risk of coronary heart disease by age 50 in men and age 60 in women.

The inheritance pattern is autosomal dominant with each offspring having a 50% risk of inheriting the pathogenic variant.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Lipid-lowering therapy should be initiated or optimized according to current FH management guidelines
2. Cascade screening is strongly recommended for first-degree relatives
3. Predictive testing is available for family members if appropriate, following genetic counseling
4. Regular cardiovascular risk assessment and monitoring
5. Lifestyle modifications including dietary management and regular exercise

This report has been authorized by:
[redacted name], PhD, FRCPath
Consultant Clinical Scientist
